workshop.statusExplain.finished1: Gratulálunk! A kemény munka után végre elérte a hihetetlen utazás végét. Habár most véget ér a történet, reméljük, hogy lesznek még újabb történetek a jövőben, de most pihenjen és élvezze az érdemelt pihenést.
workshop.statusExplain.finished2: A történet befejezettnek jelölése azt jelenti, hogy a történet befejeződött. Habár nem kell új fejezeteket hozzáadnia, mi nem akadályozzuk meg benne, és nem is rossz ötlet különleges fejezetek hozzáadása, például több epilógus hozzáadása minden szereplőnek.
workshop.statusExplain.finished3: Bár mindig visszavonhatja ezt az állapotot, erősen javasoljuk, hogy ne tegye. Ha a történet folytatódni fog, akkor talán jobb új történetet kezdeni.

workshop.timer.breakMessage: Take a moment to rest. Click anywhere to dismiss.
workshop.timer.tabInactive: Timer paused - switch back to tab to continue
workshop.timer.type.timer.desc: Simple stopwatch that starts at 0:00 and counts upward. Perfect for tracking total writing time in a session or seeing how long you've been working continuously. Never ends automatically - you control when to stop.
workshop.timer.type.countdown.desc: Countdown timer that starts from your set duration and counts down to zero. Great for time-boxed writing sessions, word sprints, or when you want to work for a specific amount of time before taking a break.
workshop.timer.type.pomodoro.desc: Structured productivity technique: 25-minute focused work sessions alternating with 5-minute breaks. After 4 cycles, takes a longer 15-30 minute break. Scientifically proven to improve focus and prevent burnout.
workshop.timer.mode.regular.desc: Timer runs continuously regardless of your activity. Best for disciplined writers who want to track time even when researching, editing, or taking short breaks. Timer keeps going when you switch tabs or stop typing.
workshop.timer.mode.improved.desc: Smart timer that automatically pauses when you switch browser tabs. Perfect for focused writing sessions where you want accurate tracking of actual writing time, not total time spent on the page.
workshop.timer.breakType.soft.desc: Gentle reminder approach: Shows a small notification when break time starts. You can choose to continue working if you're in 'the zone' or take the break. Good for flexible writers who sometimes need to extend productive sessions.
workshop.timer.breakType.hard.desc: Strict enforcement: Displays a full-screen modal that prevents further input until the break timer completes. Forces you to step away from the keyboard. Ideal for writers who struggle with self-discipline or workaholics who need enforced rest periods.
workshop.timer.duration.timer.desc: How long you plan to write in this session. Start with 25-50 minutes for focused work, or set longer sessions (2-4 hours) for deep writing days.
workshop.timer.duration.countdown.desc: Target writing time before the timer ends. Try 25 minutes for focused sprints, 45-60 minutes for substantial work sessions, or 90 minutes for creative deep dives.
workshop.timer.workDuration.desc: Length of focused work sessions. Traditional Pomodoro uses 25 minutes. Try 15-20 minutes if you find it hard to concentrate for longer periods, or 45-50 minutes for experienced writers who can maintain deep focus.
workshop.timer.breakDuration.desc: Rest period between work sessions. Standard is 5 minutes for short breaks. Use 10-15 minutes for longer breaks that allow you to step away from your desk, stretch, or get a drink. Every 4th break is automatically longer (2-3x duration).

workshop.inspiration.prompt-001: Begin with a character arriving too early for something that could change their life.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-009: Begin at the moment a plan fails in public.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-011: A routine errand becomes impossible for a reason the character cannot explain.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-020: Start with an ordinary morning and introduce one impossible detail by the third paragraph.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-021: Write a character profile built entirely from what is in their bag or pockets.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-025: Invent a character who wants admiration but mistrusts praise.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-026: Build a character around one promise they regret making.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-060: One sentence spoken at the wrong moment changes the meaning of the whole scene.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-064: Design a house that reveals its owner better than any biography could.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-065: Build a setting where weather affects memory.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-066: Describe a place of worship that has outlived the belief it was built for.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-067: Create a village where everyone knows one part of a local legend and no one knows the whole thing.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-068: Write a scene in a room that used to belong to someone important.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-069: Invent a border crossing between two places with radically different values.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-070: Describe a library section that few people visit and everyone misjudges.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-071: Build a world where silence has social meaning.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-072: Create a festival that exists to prevent something terrible from happening again.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-073: Write a landscape that appears beautiful to visitors and threatening to locals.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-074: Design a city where the oldest infrastructure still decides modern life.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-075: Describe a workshop, kitchen, lab, or forge so vividly that it suggests a plot.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-076: Invent a neighborhood where each street has a reputation and one of them is unfair.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-077: Write about a place where names are displayed, traded, hidden, or earned.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-078: Create a setting shaped by a recent absence rather than a recent event.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-079: Describe a public place moments before it becomes historic.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-080: Build a world rule that seems small but changes everyday human behavior.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-082: Someone must betray a friend to keep a larger promise.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-083: Write a victory that immediately creates a worse problem.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-084: A character discovers their enemy has been protecting them.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-085: Create a scene where the safest choice is morally unacceptable.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-086: A long-awaited inheritance turns out to be an obligation.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-087: Write a story in which the evidence is true but misleading.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-095: A promise made in childhood becomes binding in adulthood.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-102: Magic disappears for one hour every week, and someone has learned to use that hour.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-103: Write about a city powered by a resource people can only produce sincerely.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-104: A translator discovers a language that changes the speaker more than the listener.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-105: Every family guards one impossible object; one family has lost theirs.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-106: A child can hear the arguments of machines.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-107: Time travel exists, but only for emotional emergencies.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-108: Write a romance between two people who meet in different versions of the same city.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-110: An expedition finds a place mapped in folklore but absent from history.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-111: People can temporarily borrow skills, but the lender loses more than expected.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-112: Write about an artificial intelligence trained on banned literature.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-113: A healer can mend any wound except the first one they ever saw.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-114: In a world of visible auras, one character’s aura is unreadable.

workshop.inspiration.prompt-124: Explore the cost of being the reliable one in every relationship.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-125: Write about a family story everyone tells proudly except the person who lived it.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-126: Describe success arriving in a form your character did not want.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-127: Write about the private loneliness of a very competent person.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-128: A character returns an item they have no right to keep and every right to resent giving back.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-129: Write a scene where forgiveness is offered before understanding.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-130: Explore what changes when a character is finally seen accurately.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-131: Write about the first time a parent asks a child for advice.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-132: A character is praised for a sacrifice no one noticed they never agreed to make.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-133: Write a goodbye between two people who will almost certainly meet again.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-134: Explore the emotional difference between being chosen and being needed.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-135: Write about a friendship strained not by betrayal but by uneven growth.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-136: A character tells the truth for once and discovers the lie had been protecting others.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-137: Write about a person who has become what they once judged harshly.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-138: Explore the relief of disappointing the right person.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-139: Write a scene where grief and gratitude arrive together.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-140: A character is offered a second chance at something they no longer trust themselves to want.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-141: Tell a complete story backward, beginning with the consequence.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-142: Write a scene entirely through text messages, notes, or official messages.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-143: Tell a tense moment from the viewpoint of someone who misunderstands it.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-144: Write a story where the narrator refuses to describe the central event.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-145: Rewrite the same scene from the perspectives of the most powerful and least powerful people present.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-146: Tell a story using only one location and one interruption.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-147: Write a scene with no dialogue in which the relationship still changes.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-148: Use second person for a character who hates being told what to do.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-149: Tell a story in which the reader learns the secret before the protagonist does.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-150: Write a first chapter that promises one genre and a second chapter that reveals another.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-151: Compose a scene where every paragraph shortens the emotional distance between characters.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-152: Write a story in exactly nine sentences, with the ninth sentence changing the meaning of the first.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-153: Tell a scene through what is overheard from the next room.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-154: Write a chapter where no one lies, but nearly everything is misleading.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-155: Use an unreliable narrator who is unreliable because they are hopeful, not deceptive.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-156: Tell a story through a sequence of objects changing owners.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-157: Write a scene where the setting is described only through smell, sound, touch, and taste.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-158: Compose a monologue that begins as explanation and ends as confession.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-159: Tell a story in which the protagonist never appears directly on the page.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-160: Write an ending first, then create the opening that makes it inevitable.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-161: Set a timer for three minutes and list ten things your protagonist is afraid to lose.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-162: Write five surprising comparisons for rain, hunger, ambition, silence, or regret.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-163: Describe the room you are in as if your main character has just entered it for the first time.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-164: Write one line each of dialogue for a king, a thief, a child, and a widow without naming them.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-165: List five secrets a town could keep and choose the quietest one to build a story around.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-166: Write the worst possible first sentence for a novel, then rewrite it into a strong first sentence.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-167: Name three objects on your desk and invent a history that connects them.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-168: Write a 100-word scene in which someone wants something badly but asks for something else.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-169: Take a cliché and flip the power dynamic inside it.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-170: Write a description of a meal that reveals a conflict.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-171: Draft three titles for stories that do not exist yet, then pick the most dangerous one.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-172: Write a character introduction that includes one contradiction.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-173: Create a map of a home, ship, school, or station and mark where a secret is hidden.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-174: Write a paragraph that begins calm and ends uneasy without mentioning danger.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-175: Invent a superstition and show one person obeying it and another exploiting it.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-176: Write a scene opener that includes weather, a goal, and a lie.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-177: Choose a public place and list what different characters would notice first.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-178: Write a seven-line exchange where status shifts without anyone acknowledging it.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-179: Turn a boring task into a dramatic scene by raising one emotional stake.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-180: Finish this sentence three different ways: “By morning, everyone agreed that the letter had changed everything.”
workshop.inspiration.prompt-181: Write for five minutes about what your current project is really about beneath the plot.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-182: Make a list of ten scenes you would love to write even if they never make the final book.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-183: Write a letter from your protagonist to you, complaining about your choices as the author.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-184: Identify the emotional weather of your story and describe it without using mood words.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-185: Write the scene you keep avoiding and allow it to be messy.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-186: Take a stalled chapter and write the version in which the most honest person tells the truth too early.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-187: Ask, “What would make this harder?” and answer it five times for your current story.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-188: Write a paragraph on what your antagonist protects, not just what they want.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-189: Describe your story’s world from the perspective of someone who hates it.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-190: Rewrite your premise as a folktale, a headline, and a prayer.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-191: Write down three moral lines your protagonist will not cross, then break one.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-192: List ten things your character notices when afraid and ten things they miss.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-193: Write a version of your central relationship in which the power balance is reversed.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-194: Distill your novel idea into one promise, one wound, and one irreversible choice.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-195: Write the happiest possible version of your story idea, then steal one thing from it for the darker version.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-196: Draft a scene where your protagonist fails with dignity.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-197: Write the moment before the story begins: the last ordinary second.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-198: Give your project a hidden theme and write three symbols that could carry it.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-199: Describe the cost of your story’s ending before you decide whether it is worth paying.
workshop.inspiration.prompt-200: Write one paragraph answering this question: why does this story deserve years of your life?
workshop.inspiration.title: A spark for your next page
workshop.inspiration.intro: Try this week's shared prompt, or draw another from our curated collection.
workshop.inspiration.upgrade: Save prompts for later with Adventurer or Storyteller.
workshop.inspiration.error: Your saved prompts could not be updated. Please try again.
workshop.inspiration.empty: Save a prompt when you'd like to come back to it.
workshop.universe.notes.title: Universe notes for {universeTitle}
workshop.universe.notes.desc: Keep your imported card values visible while outlining the foundations, tensions, and story potential of this universe.
workshop.universe.notes.cardsUnavailable: The card import is attached to this universe, but no card groups were provided in the imported payload.
workshop.universe.notes.noForgeImport: This universe does not have Universe Cards data attached yet.
forgeUniverse.connect.import.missingSele: Select a universe before importing the world data.
forgeUniverse.connect.import.confirmRequ: Confirm the overwrite before replacing the existing universe notes.
forgeUniverse.connect.title: Connect your world
forgeUniverse.connect.missing: We could not find the imported Universe Cards data. Please reopen Literary Universe from the Universe Cards app and try again.
forgeUniverse.connect.desc: Choose whether to start a brand-new universe from this Universe Cards session, or attach the imported world data to one of your existing universes.
forgeUniverse.connect.createDesc: Start a fresh universe in the workshop and carry the card values straight into the new universe notes page.
forgeUniverse.connect.existingDesc: Import this Universe Cards session into one of your current universes and continue from its universe notes page.
forgeUniverse.connect.existingOverwriteW: This universe already has imported cards or universe notes. Importing this draft will replace the current imported values and clear the existing universe note outline.
forgeUniverse.connect.existingOverwriteC: I understand that the existing universe notes will be overwritten.
forgeUniverse.connect.noUniverses: You do not have any existing universes available yet. Create a new one from this Universe Cards session.
workshop.universe.forgeImportNotice: Your Universe Cards values and notes will be attached to this universe when you save it.
workshop.creation.title: What would you like to create?
workshop.creation.intro: Choose what fits your idea. We'll guide you through the first few decisions and create a draft. Nothing is published until you choose to publish it.
workshop.creation.story.help: Start with one story. Write chapters, arrange scenes, and publish when you are ready. You can add a universe later.
workshop.creation.universe.help: Build a shared world for your stories. Keep characters, places, and world rules in its encyclopedia, then add stories set there.
workshop.creation.fanfiction.help: Write a story set in someone else’s universe. Choose an eligible universe from your library and follow its permissions.
workshop.creation.comic.help: Tell a story through sequential art. Choose comic, manga, or a scrolling webtoon, then add chapters and pages.
workshop.creation.basics.help: Give your idea a working title and a short description. You can change these later. The slug is the readable part of its web address.
workshop.creation.details.help: Choose a genre and an age rating so readers know what to expect. Your license controls how others may use your work. The license helper explains the options before you choose.
workshop.creation.draft.help: This creates an unpublished draft. You can add a cover, collaborators, and more settings in your workshop before publishing.
workshop.import.help: Bring a Word document or a compiled Scrivener manuscript into a new story draft. Review the chapters, then choose the story’s language, rating and license.
workshop.import.formats: DOCX, Markdown and text are supported. In Word or Scrivener Compile, use Heading 1 for chapter titles. Legacy DOC, PDF, EPUB, native Scrivener projects and service account archives are not supported here.
workshop.import.formatting: Paragraphs, headings, emphasis, lists and tables are retained where possible. Images, page layout and unsupported formatting are omitted. Check the preview before importing. Files are read in your browser; only the reviewed chapters are sent when you import.
workshop.import.warnings: The document converter reported {count, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}. Check the preview for unsupported formatting.
workshop.import.draftNotice: The story and all chapters stay unpublished. Existing stories are never overwritten. Retrying an identical import in this tab returns the same draft.
workshop.import.failed: The import did not finish. Check your details and try again. Retrying the same import resumes its existing draft; saved chapters are kept.
workshop.import.readFailed: This file could not be read. Choose a DOCX, Markdown or text document up to 10 MB, with readable text and no more than 200 chapters.
workshop.import.splitFailed: This split leaves empty or too many chapters. Choose a different split.
workshop.import.chapterCount: {count, plural, one {# chapter} other {# chapters}} will be created in this order.
series.title: Series
series.recover: A previous save did not finish. Review this saved plan and save again to finish creating its drafts.
series.name: Series title
series.help: Arrange stories and connect them in reading order. New stories become unpublished drafts when you save. They inherit this universe’s language, genre, rating, and license.
series.deleteDraft: Also delete this unpublished draft when I save
series.morePlanned: More stories are planned for this series.
universe.notes.readOnly: You can read these notes. Editing is available to universe collaborators and organization administrators.
forgeUniverse.connect.verifyEmail: Verify your email before creating or importing a universe. Your world is saved in this browser. Open the verification link here, then choose Continue to return to your world.
forgeUniverse.connect.verificationSent: Verification email sent. Check your inbox.
